newsitem.title: USA: Most US debt futures end steady, erase daily gains.
newsitem.headline: Most US debt futures end steady, erase daily gains.

text.p: U.S. debt futures closed mostly unchanged after the market erased the day's gains on long liquidation, traders and analysts said.

"We are trying to probe for a new range," Larry Berman, senior technical analyst at Technical Data, said, adding that December bonds USZ6 would probably carve out a range between the upper-111-00 handle and 114-00.
"That is going to bind us for the next couple of weeks," he said. "You have the potential for bullish data, but you also have supply pressures coming up."
The Federal Reserve's Beige Book gave traders who became extremely long in the 112-00 handle on Tuesday and early Wednesday an excuse to take profits, traders and analysts said.
The Fed's summary of economic activity from September to October 22 said the pace of U.S. growth has slowed somewhat but wage pressures are rising.
The Fed also said price rises remain limited despite a "proliferation" of wage increases.
December T-bonds gravitated below the previous intraday low of 112-14/32 and through support at 112-10/32.

However, traders said the summary did not change expectations -- born out of Tuesday's U.S. third-quarter employment cost index -- that the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) would remain on hold at November's meeting.
"The market is a little overbought near term, but it's okay," one floor trader said.

They said the short-end of the market is even more limited on the upside, as December EDZ6 brushed briefly over 94.51. Resistance for December is seen at 5.50 percent, as the three-month LIBOR rate of 5.50 percent.

September personal income and consumption data will be released at 0830 EST/1330 GMT on Thursday. Income is seen rising 0.6 percent, the same as in August, and consumption is forecast to rise 0.3 percent, versus a 0.6 percent rise in August.

At the end of pit trade, December T-bonds were steady at 112-19/32, 10-year notes were unchanged at 109-14/32, munibonds were up 07/32 at 115-08/32, March Eurodollars were down one basis point at 94.42, June Eurodollars were also down one basis point at 94.31 and March T-bills fell one basis point at 94.92.
